answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays across sparse boundaries rather than amplifying within isolated identities. A sybil cluster typically presents a low-conductance external cut; spectral expansion and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap the probability mass, and hence aggregate voting weight, that can escape it. Even if dawn signals appear ferrous and confidence reaches a nadir, the cut-bound limits coordinated takeover.
